meta.title: Mongolian Alphabet
meta.subtitle: 35 letters and the long vowel · both directions, as two cards each
meta.desc: The 35 letters of the Mongolian Cyrillic alphabet, in alphabetical order — Russian's 33 and Ө and Ү — and then the long vowel: the first deck of the Mongolian collection, since the level decks are written in Cyrillic from their first card and carry no romanisation. Both directions: see a letter and recall its sound, or see a sound and recall the letter, each a card with its own schedule. Every note gives the letter in capital and small, its name (what a Mongolian calls it when spelling a word aloud), its sound described in English words with the IPA and the standard romanisation beside it, and one everyday word that shows it. The sounds are approximations, as every learner's alphabet gives them; where English has no near equivalent, as for л, ө and the rolled р, the card says so. Several letters are not said as in Russian: б and д have no voice, ж and з are said like an unvoiced j and ts, в is between v and w, and л is a hissed l. Ф and к are letters of borrowed words, щ is written only in Russian ones, and the hard and soft signs have no sound of their own. Sources: the names, IPA and romanisation (MNS 5217:2012) are read from the table of Wikipedia's 'Mongolian Cyrillic alphabet' (revision 1380007835, CC BY-SA 4.0), whose IPA cites Svantesson et al., The Phonology of Mongolian (2005); the example words and their meanings are cards of the A1 deck, from English Wiktionary (CC BY-SA 4.0). There is no speaker button: few devices have a Mongolian voice.

fields.Name: а
fields.Sound: "a" as in father

fields.Name: бэ
fields.Sound: a "b" said without voice, between the b of bat and the p of spin

fields.Name: вэ
fields.Sound: between English v and w, made with both lips

fields.Name: гэ
fields.Sound: "g" as in go; in a word with а, о or у, said further back in the throat

fields.Name: дэ
fields.Sound: a "d" said without voice, like the t of stop

fields.Name: е
fields.Sound: "yi" or "yö" (a y, then a short rounded vowel); after a consonant the y is not heard and the consonant is softened

fields.Name: ё
fields.Sound: "yo" as in yonder; after a consonant the y is not heard and the consonant is softened

fields.Name: жэ
fields.Sound: like the j of jam, but without voice: between j and ch

fields.Name: зэ
fields.Sound: like the ts of cats, but without the puff of breath (romanised z or dz)

fields.Name: и
fields.Sound: "ee" as in meet; after a consonant it also softens it

fields.Name: хагас и
fields.Sound: a short i, the y of boy, written after a vowel (ай, ой, үй)

fields.Name: ка
fields.Sound: "k" as in kite; a letter of borrowed words, often said as х

fields.Name: эл
fields.Sound: the tongue set for an l while the breath hisses past its sides, like the Welsh ll; English has no equivalent

fields.Name: эм
fields.Sound: "m" as in man

fields.Name: эн
fields.Sound: "n" as in no; at the end of a word, the ng of sing

fields.Name: о
fields.Sound: an open "o", as in British hot, held

fields.Name: ө
fields.Sound: a rounded vowel like the u of fur said with rounded lips (German ö); English has no equivalent

fields.Name: пэ
fields.Sound: "p" as in pen, with a puff of breath

fields.Name: эр
fields.Sound: a rolled "r", made with the tip of the tongue; English has no equivalent

fields.Name: эс
fields.Sound: "s" as in sun

fields.Name: тэ
fields.Sound: "t" as in top, with a puff of breath

fields.Name: у
fields.Sound: "u" as in put

fields.Name: ү
fields.Sound: "oo" as in food, the tongue higher and further forward than for у

fields.Name: фэ, фа, эф
fields.Sound: "f" as in fun; a letter of borrowed words, often said as п

fields.Name: хэ, ха
fields.Sound: "kh", like the ch of Scottish loch

fields.Name: цэ
fields.Sound: "ts" as in cats, with a puff of breath

fields.Name: чэ
fields.Sound: "ch" as in chop, with a puff of breath

fields.Name: ша, эш
fields.Sound: "sh" as in shop

fields.Name: ща, эщэ
fields.Sound: written only in Russian words, and said as ш

fields.Name: хатуугийн тэмдэг
fields.Sound: the hard sign: no sound of its own

fields.Name: эр үгийн ы
fields.Sound: "ee" as in meet, written in the endings of a word with а, о or у

fields.Name: зөөлний тэмдэг
fields.Sound: the soft sign: no sound of its own; it softens the consonant before it

fields.Name: э
fields.Sound: "e" as in met

fields.Name: ю
fields.Sound: "yu" as in you

fields.Name: я
fields.Sound: "ya" as in yard

fields.Letter: аа ээ оо өө уу үү
fields.Name: урт эгшиг
fields.Sound: a vowel written twice is long: the same vowel, held
